candidates.statement: CALIPER is described as an age- and sex-specific pediatric reference-interval database covering more than 200 tests, serving as a new candidate locator for actual CALIPER interval values including CBC parameters.
candidates.quote: The public CALIPER database is the strongest new candidate for **RF-EV-002** because it is described as an age- and sex-specific pediatric reference-interval database covering more than 200 tests.
candidates.selector_value: age- and sex-specific pediatric reference-interval database

candidates.statement: The database page itself does not establish that every desired CBC parameter is available for each analyzer or that its values carry an open reuse license.
candidates.quote: The database page itself does **not** establish, in the retrieved result, that every desired CBC parameter is available for each analyzer or that its values carry an open reuse license.
candidates.selector_value: its values carry an open reuse license

candidates.statement: Age-banded WBC plus differential—the Iowa, UVM, ABPath, and CALIPER candidates are the highest-yield numeric locators found; the UVM document specifically advertises WBC, differential cell counts, platelets, hematocrit, hemoglobin, and reticulocyte pediatric ranges.
candidates.quote: the Iowa, UVM, ABPath, and CALIPER candidates are the highest-yield numeric locators found here; the UVM document specifically advertises WBC, differential cell counts, platelets, hematocrit, hemoglobin, and reticulocyte pediatric ranges.

candidates.statement: ANC benign versus severe neutropenia remains a gap in the net-new list because the best directly relevant open pediatric review is already held in the bundle and therefore was intentionally not resurfaced.
candidates.quote: **ANC benign versus severe neutropenia:** this remains a gap in the *net-new* list because the best directly relevant open pediatric review is already held in the bundle and therefore was intentionally not resurfaced.

candidates.statement: Platelet severity/action bands from CPS and Royal Cornwall sources give useful accessible count-context statements, but neither should be represented as a universal platelet-only action policy; both make bleeding severity clinically material.
candidates.quote: the CPS and Royal Cornwall sources give useful accessible count-context statements, but neither should be represented as a universal platelet-only action policy; both make bleeding severity clinically material.
candidates.selector_value: neither should be represented as a universal platelet-only action policy

candidates.statement: Leukemoid reaction versus blasts: no pediatric-specific, independently retrievable numeric leukemoid/blast-referral passage was identified in this sweep.

candidates.statement: WBC age bands from Iowa source: 0–1 month 9,000–30,000/mm3; 1–3 months 5,000–19,500/mm3; 3 months–1 year 6,000–17,500/mm3; 1–2 years 6,000–17,000/mm3; and 2–4 years 5,500–15,500/mm3.
candidates.quote: **Yes—WBC age bands**, including 0–1 month 9,000–30,000/mm3; 1–3 months 5,000–19,500/mm3; 3 months–1 year 6,000–17,500/mm3; 1–2 years 6,000–17,000/mm3; and 2–4 years 5,500–15,500/mm3.

candidates.statement: Hypereosinophilia is defined as AEC at or above 1,500 cells/uL, equivalent to 1.5 10*9/L, serving as a eosinophilia pattern and numeric referral/work-up trigger.
candidates.quote: **Yes—hypereosinophilia is defined as AEC at or above 1,500 cells/uL**, equivalent to 1.5 `10*9/L`.

candidates.statement: WHO persistent monocytosis definition: absolute monocytes above 1 10*9/L, more than 10% of leukocytes, persisting more than 3 months.
candidates.qualifier_band: absolute monocyte count persistence (>3 months, >10% differential)
candidates.quote: WHO persistent monocytosis definition: absolute monocytes above 1 `10*9/L`, more than 10% of leukocytes, persisting more than 3 months.

candidates.statement: WBC above 11,000 cells/uL is described as general leukocytosis, while the source expressly notes that normal limits vary by age and physiologic state.
candidates.quote: **Yes—WBC above 11,000 cells/uL is described as general leukocytosis**, while the source expressly notes that normal limits vary by age and physiologic state.

candidates.statement: The ITP guideline states that low platelet counts alone, including counts below 10 10*9/L, are not themselves an indication for treatment.
candidates.qualifier_band: platelet count action context (treatment not indicated by count alone)
candidates.quote: the guideline states that low platelet counts alone, including counts below 10 `10*9/L`, are not themselves an indication for treatment.

candidates.statement: Isolated thrombocytopenia below 100,000/uL is stated as the diagnostic count criterion for ITP as described by the comprehensive review.
candidates.qualifier_band: platelet count diagnostic criterion for ITP
candidates.quote: **Yes—isolated thrombocytopenia below 100,000/uL** is stated as the diagnostic count criterion described by the review.

candidates.statement: Some experts use platelet counts above 10 or 20 10*9/L as hemostatic targets; the document also states that management is driven by bleeding severity rather than count alone.
candidates.qualifier_band: platelet count hemostatic target (expert opinion, bleeding-severity dependent)
candidates.quote: some experts use platelet counts above 10 or 20 `10*9/L` as hemostatic targets; the document also states that management is driven by bleeding severity rather than count alone.
